subject: On Mission
body_text:
View this post on the web at https://rebeccachoi1.substack.com/p/on-mission

During Spring Break, 15 students and 3 post-grad staff went to the Dominican Republic for a Filter of Hope mission trip. As part of our partnership with Filter of Hope, we partnered with a local church to bring people 1) the gift of clean water through a powerful water filter that can last up to 10 years, and 2) the gift of eternal life through the gospel.
Even though there wasn’t as much of an emotional high, I can confidently say that it left an immensly profound impact on my understanding of how we are to live as Christians, therefore (probably) shaping the way I am going to live my life going forward.
My Attitude There
The main component to our visits in each of the houses was the gift of the gospel. Before every house we went to, I found myself praying to God for the gospel to be delivered to whoever we were going to meet in a way very personal to them. I reviewed different Bible verses that addressed common barriers to believing. I mentally prepared myself to stay alert and focused since I was often tired and distracted by the heat.
When I was there, I was fully living off the truth that the gospel was the single most important truth for both our team and for anyone we were going to meet. Tired? Doesn’t matter. Lock in. Personality clashes within the team? Figure it out before it becomes a barrier to us delivering the gospel. The gospel single-handedly nullified anyone’s personal desires or beliefs. Its message was simple and its power, clear.
A Shift In Perspective
The real realization happened after the mission trip when I started thinking about my own non-Christian friends. How come I didn’t have the same attitude with the gospel back in Boston? How come I lived with seemingly far less assurance in the gospel message back in the states? Less urgency, more excuses. We’re not close enough. I’m gonna make them uncomfortable.
However, the gospel is not any less true here nor is it any less relevant to my friends as it is to the people in the DR. God is not at any less work here than there. And we are not any less called to be servants of God, vessels of His word and love, here than we were there. The peace we have in Jesus is not any less real when we have our own personal difficulties (John 14), and the God we praised for the souls saved and seeds planted there is the same God that saved us and who we can hope in to work in lives here.
Thus, the trip became a way to remember what is true. It’s such a no-brainer but I never thought about it like that. I’m technically on mission right now. We all are, regardless of where we are and who is around us. Me being here living the way I am is like as if I committed to a mission trip and I spent most of my time traveling and getting comfortable. Lock in!!
How It’s Different
Now that I kind of understand the nuances of clearly articulating the different components of the gospel a little bit better, hopefully I can put all that I’ve learned into practice in Boston now.
Obviously it’s kind of different when we are in our more permanent homes. You probably won’t treat a short-term mission trip the same way you would a lifelong one. The pacing would be slightly different and in “lifelong mission trips” you have more options for how to deliver the gospel, like you can be more relational with it instead of just saying it. It’s these kinds of nuances that I think I still need to figure out, but regardless of the methodology, the essence is the same.
I’ve been thinking a lot about: what can I do to maximize the impact the mission trip has on my life here, and it’s pretty clear: just don’t stop. Don’t let the mission trip be over. It’s still going! It doesn’t take a clear-cut ministry plan for how I want to serve God, and the perfect balance between work and ministry. Work, ministry, hobbies, friends, they can and should all be intertwined. Wherever I am, whatever I’m doing, there is opportunity to glorify and serve God. It’s the same mission wherever you are. It’s not the place, not the plan, but simply an open heart and willingness.
It’s God’s responsibility to save.
It’s our responsibility to share.
It’s their responsibility to believe.

subject: Scaling Trino Simply  🌐,  Snowflake Join Trap  🐌,  Death of BI Layers 📉
body_text:
Trino Gateway solves the growing complexity of managing dozens of
specialized clusters as query volume, concurrency, and workload
diversity
explode                                                      


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

 TLDR 

 TOGETHER WITH [Databricks] [4]

TLDR DATA 2026-03-26

 “THE DATABASE IS STILL PROVISIONING? SURE, I'D LOVE TO WAIT
LONGER,” SAID NO ONE EVER.  SKIP THE WAIT AND GET TO THE REAL WORK
WITH LAKEBASE. (SPONSOR) [4] 

 Lakebase is a serverless Postgres DB that lets you branch your whole
DB almost instantly. Run tests on prod data, spin up AI apps, and
more. With separate storage and compute, you wait less and build
faster. 

With Lakebase you can: 

	* Branch databases for testing 
	* Scale up fast — and down to zero just as easily
	* Run apps, agents and AI on one database
	* Use one database for operational and analytical data

Get the Databricks founders' rundown on Lakebase [4], jump straight to
building [5] or watch a walk-through [6]. The choice is yours. 

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 WHY YOUR SNOWFLAKE JOINS ARE SLOW: FIX OR JOINS FAST (12 MINUTE READ)
[7] 

 Disjunctive joins (using OR in join conditions) break Snowflake's
hash join optimization, forcing expensive Cartesian products and
massive performance slowdowns. The fix is to rewrite them as separate
equi-joins, restoring efficient execution and often delivering
100–200x speedups. 

 VOLGA - DATA PROCESSING FOR REAL-TIME AI/ML (20 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Volga is now a fully Rust-based engine for real-time AI/ML, replacing
the earlier Python+Ray core to get a simpler, higher-performance
runtime and tighter control over execution and state. It unifies
streaming, batch, and request-time compute in one standalone system,
aiming to eliminate the usual stitching across Flink, Spark, Redis,
and custom services while keeping point-in-time-correct state inside
the engine. The key building blocks are Apache DataFusion for SQL
pipelines, Apache Arrow for execution semantics, and SlateDB for
S3-backed state. 

 BEYOND THE VECTOR STORE: BUILDING THE FULL DATA LAYER FOR AI
APPLICATIONS (7 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Relying solely on a vector database is no longer sufficient for
production AI applications, especially RAG, and agentic systems. A
complete AI data layer requires five integrated components: vector
store, metadata & filtering, graph layer, cache, and governance &
observability, making hybrid architectures (vector + graph +
relational) essential for achieving better accuracy, lower cost, and
true production readiness. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 FUTURE CASTING THE MODERN DATA STACK (20 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 AI-driven advancements are fundamentally challenging the Modern Data
Stack model, with LLMs now capable of generating high-quality SQL,
automating ETL pipelines, and creating sophisticated data
visualizations, drastically reducing manual query-writing and
traditional BI tool usage. Data warehouse vendors face commoditization
pressures, while consolidation and integration across the stack
accelerate. The emerging data platform paradigm is likely an agent
swarm for data management backed by a query engine powering the
analytics. 

 DATABRICKS METRIC VIEWS AND THE REALITY OF THE SEMANTIC LAYER (5
MINUTE READ) [11] 

 Databricks is entering the semantic layer space with Metric Views, a
way to centrally define business metrics directly in Unity Catalog on
top of Delta tables. However, it's still quite limited compared to
mature semantic layers, supporting only simple aggregations, and lacks
complex business logic, calculated metrics with dependencies, and
advanced dimensional modeling. 

 WHERE IS THE RIGHT PLACE TO CATCH DATA VOLUME ANOMALIES? (6 MINUTE
READ) [12] 

 Monitoring data volume anomalies at the data warehouse layer (rather
than solely at the source) is critical when sources are diverse,
failure modes are silent, and real-time streams lack batch boundaries.
This centralized approach creates a unified detection and
communication point, bridging upstream producers and downstream
consumers while providing actionable data health signals. Introducing
a suppression layer for known, context-specific anomalies minimizes
alert fatigue without incurring technical debt. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 OPERATING TRINO AT SCALE WITH TRINO GATEWAY (9 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 Expedia built Trino Gateway to solve the growing complexity of
managing dozens of specialized clusters as query volume, concurrency,
and workload diversity exploded. Instead of forcing users to connect
to different endpoints, the gateway provides a single unified
connection URL that automatically routes queries to the best cluster
based on smart rules. 

 WHEN UPSERTS DON'T UPDATE BUT STILL WRITE: DEBUGGING POSTGRES
PERFORMANCE AT SCALE (11 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Datadog hit a surprising Postgres performance issue while cleaning up
millions of ephemeral hosts: a simple upsert to update the "last seen"
timestamp doubled disk writes and quadrupled WAL syncs. The cause was
ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE always acquires a row lock and writes to the
WAL, even when no data actually changes. The fix is to avoid locking
on no-op upserts. 

 APACHE ICEBERG RUST 0.9.0 RELEASE (2 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Apache Iceberg has released iceberg-rust 0.9.0, introducing a
trait-based storage architecture that decouples the library from
specific storage backends, facilitating easier integration and
extension. This version features major performance improvements for
Arrow reads, expanded DataFusion support, and upgrades decimal
handling to 38-digit precision with the fastnum crate. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 THE DEATH OF MODEL.FIT(): WHAT DATA SCIENTISTS ACTUALLY DO IN THE AGE
OF AI AGENTS (12 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 Data science work focused on building and tuning models is rapidly
becoming obsolete as AI agents and foundation models take over.
Today's data scientists instead focus on four higher-level
responsibilities: defining business problems and metrics, designing
evaluation frameworks and guardrails, curating high-quality data, and
building reliable agent systems with prompts, tools, and human
oversight. 

 WHAT COVID DID TO OUR FORECASTING MODELS (12 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 The COVID-19 pandemic completely broke Airbnb's demand forecasting
models in March 2020. The models, trained on stable historical
patterns, failed to handle massive swings in booking volume,
unpredictable cancellation spikes, and the collapse of the normal
relationship between booking date and travel date (lead-time
composition). To solve this, Airbnb decoupled forecasting into two
separate parts: gross booking metrics on the booking-date axis and
lead-time composition (the proportion of bookings that turn into trips
on different future dates). 

 STATE OF CONTEXT ENGINEERING IN 2026 (10 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 Context engineering has rapidly become central to AI agent design.
Matured patterns, like progressive disclosure, sliding-window
compression with summarization, precise context routing, agentic
retrieval-augmented generation, and rigorous tool management, are now
broadly adopted across platforms. Anthropic's Agent Skills and the MCP
protocol have set standards for LLM-driven workflows, but tradeoffs
around token cost, latency, and maintainability persist. Data teams
should audit token consumption and implement hybrid compression and
routing early to ensure agent reliability and cost efficiency. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 QL, TYPESCRIPT, AND AGENTS (6 MINUTE READ) [19] 

 dbt's Fusion engine delivers a TypeScript-like transformation for SQL
development, introducing a type system and language server that
provide real-time type checking, intelligent autocomplete, inline
lineage, and automated refactoring across heterogeneous data
warehouses. 

 WHY DATA ENGINEERS SHOULD CARE ABOUT PYDANTIC (5 MINUTE READ) [20] 

 Pydantic v2's fast, declarative validation turns implicit data
contracts into explicit schema checks for Python pipelines.

subject: Code Mode Tooling  ⚙️,  Agentic BI Evaluation Gaps  ⚠️, GitHub’s  Search Architecture  🔎
body_text:
The code mode pattern improves MCP tool usage by having the LLM write
and execute a script that composes multiple tools in a
sandbox                                                      


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

 TLDR 

 TOGETHER WITH [Starburst] [4]

TLDR DATA 2026-03-05

 THE WAY PEOPLE ASK QUESTIONS HAS CHANGED. CAN YOUR ANALYTICS STACK
GIVE ANSWERS? (SPONSOR) [4] 

 Dashboards were built for predefined questions and scheduled updates.
But when every new question becomes a ticket, analytics slows the
business.

With AIDA, Starburst's AI data assistant [4], everyone from analysts
to CEOs can explore enterprise data in plain language, run complex
analyses, and apply their own business rules in real time. 

✅ No SQL

✅ No tickets

✅ No BI backlog [4]

Ask a question, get an answer. Skip the dashboard. Keep going.

Get a demo → [4]

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 HOW WE REBUILT THE SEARCH ARCHITECTURE FOR HIGH AVAILABILITY IN
GITHUB ENTERPRISE SERVER (5 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 GitHub rebuilt the search architecture using Elasticsearch's Cross
Cluster Replication (CCR) to run independent single-node clusters per
instance (primary and replicas), enabling durable persistence,
asynchronous replication triggered after Lucene segments are created,
custom workflows for setup and failover management, zero-downtime
migrations, and automatic replica promotion for failover. 

 OPTIMIZING RECOMMENDATION SYSTEMS WITH JDK'S VECTOR API (9 MINUTE
READ) [6] 

 Netflix reduced CPU utilization for its Ranker service's serendipity
scoring feature from 7.5% to ~1% per node by re-architecting its
scoring logic. Key optimizations included transitioning from O(M×N)
scalar dot products to batched, cache-friendly matrix multiplies with
flat buffers, leveraging the JDK Vector API for SIMD performance gains
in pure Java, and eliminating unnecessary allocations. These changes
yielded a 7% CPU drop, 12% latency reduction, and 10% improvement in
CPU/RPS. 

 ZERO-WASTE AGENTIC RAG: DESIGNING CACHING ARCHITECTURES TO MINIMIZE
LATENCY AND LLM COSTS AT SCALE (19 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 A validation-aware, two-tier caching strategy for production-grade
RAG systems reduces LLM token costs by over 30% and slashes response
times from ~36 seconds to milliseconds for semantically similar
queries. Combining semantic caching (embedding-based, ~95% similarity)
and retrieval caching (context/topic-level, >70%), the architecture
addresses redundancy, data staleness, and cache invalidation via
timestamp checks, SHA-256 fingerprinting, and predicate caching. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 SQL IS SOLVED. HERE'S WHERE CHAT-BI STILL BREAKS (7 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Empirical testing of agentic chat-BI systems using BIRD and DABStep
benchmarks revealed high SQL generation accuracy (over 70% correct on
BIRD) but exposed critical failure nodes: ambiguous metric
definitions, out-of-scope questions, and common-sense gaps. Context
and rule files (e.g., RULES.md) help but induce compounding errors and
overfitting as complexity grows. Iterative human-in-the-loop
evaluation, structured error classification, deterministic metric
definitions, and reproducible CI testing are essential for
reliability. 

 THE RECKONING IS ALREADY HERE (3 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 AI tools are already replacing a lot of routine data engineering and
analytics work right now (not in the future), so prioritize deep
business understanding, irreplaceable domain expertise, strong
community ties, and staying ahead by mastering the newest AI models. 

 LAYER BY LAYER, WE BUILT DATA SYSTEMS NO ONE UNDERSTANDS (6 MINUTE
READ) [10] 

 The modern data stack has evolved into incomprehensible "fractal"
complexity through endless layering of tools, driven by promises of
"ease" that enable rapid prototyping but foster departmental silos,
decision avoidance, unchecked AI/LLM code generation, business logic
over-modeling, and disconnection from real business value. 

 HOW LONG UNTIL WE CALL AI AGENTS DATA PRODUCTS (7 MINUTE READ) [11] 

 AI agents in production must be managed as full-fledged data
products, requiring rigorous observability, security, and iterative
product analytics beyond standard logging. Treating agent interactions
as actionable feedback loops drives roadmap decisions, while layered
security and conversational discoverability are essential for user
trust and adoption. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 STOP CALLING TOOLS, START WRITING CODE (MODE) (8 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 The code mode pattern improves MCP tool usage by having the LLM write
and execute a script that composes multiple tools in a sandbox,
instead of calling tools sequentially. This reduces context window
bloat and round-trip overhead, making large tool catalogs far more
scalable and efficient for LLMs to use. 

 POSTGRESQL BLINK-TREE IMPLEMENTATION (7 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 PostgreSQL implements a high-concurrency version of B-tree indexes
called Blink-Tree, adding a simple "link" pointer between sibling
nodes and a "high-key" boundary marker in each node. This lets
searches move quickly to the right sibling if needed without holding
locks across multiple levels (no lock-coupling during reads), while
structure changes like page splits use brief bottom-up lock-coupling
on just a few nodes at a time, reducing lock contention dramatically. 

 PGJITTER (GITHUB REPO) [14] 

 PgJitter is a lightweight PostgreSQL extension that replaces the
default LLVM JIT compiler with faster alternatives (sljit, AsmJIT, and
MIR), enabling native code generation in microseconds instead of
milliseconds. This dramatically reduces compilation overhead and makes
JIT practical for a wider range of queries, especially OLTP workloads.


🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 AI EVALS IN THE REAL WORLD: HUMAN JUDGING, LLM JUDGES, AND THE GAPS
BETWEEN (4 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Regular AI test scores don't work well for customer-service bots that
need to keep conversations going, understand hidden intent, and
actually get users to share contact info. The team built a better
scoring system that mixes human taste-testing for tricky parts with
LLM-as-judge auto-scoring for scale, plus human spot checks on bad
cases. 

 SOMETHING IS AFOOT IN THE LAND OF QWEN (5 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 The Qwen 3.5 open-weight model family from Alibaba is gaining
attention for delivering strong performance across a wide range of
model sizes, including very small models that run locally while still
supporting reasoning and multimodal tasks. However, the project's
future is uncertain after the sudden resignation of its lead
researcher and several core team members following an internal Alibaba
reorganization. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 QUEUES FOR APACHE KAFKA IS HERE: YOUR GUIDE TO GETTING STARTED IN
CONFLUENT (11 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Queues for Kafka is now generally available on Confluent Cloud and
will be released shortly on Confluent Platform, introducing queue
semantics and elastic consumer scaling natively to Kafka via KIP-932. 

 THE NEXT EVOLUTION OF DELTA - CATALOG-MANAGED TABLES (6 MINUTE READ)
[18] 

 Delta Lake 4.1.0 introduces catalog-managed tables, shifting control
from filesystem paths to a central catalog for metadata, governance,
and commits, improving discovery and cross-engine interoperability.

subject: UStrive Mentor Newsletter - March 2026
body_text:
View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/1719ad377268/march-2026-newsletter-mentor?e=6bcfe7458e)
http://app.myustrive.com

Hi Rebecca,

Welcome to the March edition of the UStrive newsletter! In case you missed it, UStrive 2.0 (http://app.myustrive.com/login) is now live. In this newsletter, you’ll find information about the new version, our latest partnership, information on university waitlist, a UStrive scholarship opportunity for your student, a virtual mock interview opportunity for your student, product updates, dates to look out for in April, and this month’s mentor & mentee highlight.

Keep reading to learn more,

The UStrive Team

UStrive 2.0

Earlier this month, we fully sunsetted UStrive 1.0 and all user data has been migrated to our new version — 2.0! You should have received an email with the subject line, "Welcome to the New UStrive Portal – Your Login Details Inside." It contains the temporary password needed to log in to the new portal. If you never received the email, no problem! Simply email us at support@ustrive.com and we'll get you up and running.

If you haven't already, please watch this quick 3-minute video that provides an overview of what 2.0 offers and how to navigate the platform:https://youtu.be/3b7eLloFDws?si=UKlRoTcsUautCu6Dhttps://youtu.be/3b7eLloFDws?si=wiB5WcckMe75NU00

Welcoming Citizens to the UStrive Mission

We are incredibly proud to celebrate our new national partnership with Citizens. By launching this initiative during National Mentoring Month, Citizens is deeply integrating mentorship into their corporate "culture of learning."

Citizens has set an ambitious goal to match their colleagues with 300 students nationwide. This commitment directly supports our ability to keep UStrive 100% free for students while providing them with mentors who can help them navigate college applications, career exploration, and everything in between.

A Moment of Impact 🌟

As we welcome these new mentors into our family from new partners and beyond, we are reminded that every great partnership starts with a single, meaningful conversation. Think back to your own journey. What is one moment where you realized you were truly making a difference for your student? Whether it was a breakthrough in a career goal or simply a session where things "clicked," we’d love to hear your story.Share your "Mentor Moment" (https://app.myustrive.com/mentor/community) in our Online Community and see the incredible impact your peers are making every day.


** Is Your Student Waitlisted?
Here’s What you Need to Know
------------------------------------------------------------

If your student is applying to selective colleges, they might find themselves on a waitlist. This means the school isn’t ready to offer them a spot right away, but there’s a chance space could open up later. Being waitlisted doesn’t mean they’re not qualified or not good enough. Many top schools receive far more qualified applicants than they can accept because they simply don’t have enough room—whether in classrooms, dining halls, or residence halls!

Click on the article below to learn how you can support your student through the process: https://ustrive.co/waitlist-article

College acceptance season is here, and we want to celebrate this huge milestone with your mentee! Whether they’re jumping for joy, tearing up, or sharing the moment with family and friends, we want to see their genuine reaction as they open their college acceptance letter.

If you have a college-bound senior as a mentee, please encourage them to record a video of themself opening their acceptance, send it to us, and 5 lucky winners will each receive $500 towards their college expenses!

Deadline to Submit their video is April 9: [Submit here (https://ustrive.typeform.com/to/Kc4202g4) ]

**Please ensure that videos are in their original format and free from any personal or company branding**

Virtual Mock Interview Event

If you have a college junior or senior as a mentee, we’ll be hosting a Virtual Mock Interview Event in partnership with Clearsulting, where they’ll be able to connect 1:1 with a professional mentor for a live mock interview and receive personalized feedback. If they’re preparing for internships, full-time roles, or upcoming interviews, this is their chance to practice in a real interview setting.

This is a great opportunity to:

• Practice answering real interview questions

• Build confidence before recruiting season

• Get actionable feedback from professionals

Event Details
* April 10, 2025
* 12:00 PM ET
* 30–45 minutes
* Virtual (Zoom)

They’ll be paired with a mentor in a breakout room for a short mock interview followed by feedback — all in a supportive, low-pressure environment.

Students can register here:https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/gapQ9Pz4TgS3z2GqU3UhfA

UStrive Product Updates


** Now You Can Control Your Notification Settings!
------------------------------------------------------------

We've added communication preferences to your account settings. You can now choose how and when you'd like to receive updates from us. Visit your UStrive Settings (http://app.myustrive.com/login) via the web portal to manage your preferences at any time.


** Mentors Can Now Request to Work With Students
------------------------------------------------------------

If you've ever been in the "Community" tab wanting to help a student who is looking for a mentor, you can now request to be their mentor! Simply click on their name, select the "Invite to Mentor" button, and the mentee will receive the request. They'll have the option to "Accept" or "Deny."

Note: If you do not see the button for a student, it is either because they have already found a mentor (mentees are currently limited to working with one mentor at a time), or their domestic/international status doesn't match what you've indicated you can help with.


** What To Look Out For in April
------------------------------------------------------------

April 9 - UStrive’s “I Got In” Scholarship Deadline (https://ustrive.typeform.com/to/Kc4202g4)

April 11 - ACT April Test Date (https://www.act.org/content/act/en/products-and-services/the-act/registration/test-dates.html)

April 17 - SAT May Registration Deadline (https://mysat.collegeboard.org/)

Scholarships

Is your mentee still looking for scholarships? It’s not too late for them to find money for college. Encourage them to visit Fastweb (https://www.fastweb.com/?utm_source=QRCode&utm_medium=Referral&utm_campaign=2025-26_EDU) or College Board’s BigFuture (https://ustrive.co/bigfuture) . Fastweb lists thousands of scholarships, and BigFuture lets them enter monthly drawings for $500 and $40,000 awards just by completing simple college‑planning steps. It’s free, easy, and could pay off big.

Tips:

Encourage them to apply for as many scholarships as possible—small amounts add up!

Help them stay organized by tracking deadlines and requirements. They can create a document within their “Mentoring” tab.

Review their applications to ensure they highlight their strengths and experiences.

Remind them to never pay for scholarship searches—scholarship scams exist!

Motivate them to start early—some scholarships open a year in advance.

Pro Tip: Local scholarships (offered by Rotary Clubs, businesses, and schools) often have fewer applicants, increasing their chances of winning!

Get More Info & Apply: Direct your mentee to the Pay for College (https://ustrive.myustrive.com/mentor/resource-hub/guides/130idkfntUGCUjYTYviPdm?guideCategory=HIGH_SCHOOL) section in our Guides tab for a full list of resources, search tools, and expert tips to help them secure funding!



** Mentor & Mentee Highlight
------------------------------------------------------------

Mentor: Ron L.

Why did you decide to join UStrive as a mentor?

I was open to volunteering and had actually applied to Big Brother Big Sister, but they took a long time to respond. At the time, I was working at Deloitte, and UStrive had a mentorship program I could participate in through the company's community contribution initiative. I also realized that UStrive had a very fast matchmaking system — I was able to get my first mentee within one week of joining and had our first video call within two weeks. This was amazing! On top of that, it was the age group I was hoping for: seniors in high school who are genuinely first-generation college students, for whom this would be their first real experience with the college journey since their parents didn't attend college.

What has been the most impactful part of mentoring with UStrive?

The most impactful part is sharing tips and techniques with students that took me many years to learn — things like understanding what HR recruiters are looking for and how to time block. These are huge for them.

If you could share any advice with other mentors, what would it be?

The most important thing is to be somewhat firm – set homework and set goals for your mentee. Your job isn't just to make your mentee feel good. Encouragement and building self-esteem have their place, but they're only temporarily useful. Real confidence and self-respect come from actual achievements, growth, and working toward goals – all of which require sacrifice and commitment. As a mentor, I set weekly homework for my mentees and hold them accountable during check-ins. When they don't follow through, I address it – not to be harsh, but because accountability is what gets them to where they want to go. It's one of the most important skills a person can develop, and one that many people genuinely lack.

Mentee: Emily C.

Why did you decide to join UStrive?

I decided to join UStrive because I needed guidance. As a first-generation college student, I didn’t have people around me who could guide me through the college journey. Finding UStrive has been such a blessing!

What has been the most impactful part of mentoring with UStrive?

There are so many impactful parts of mentoring with UStrive, but the most impactful part has been having a mentor who believes in my potential. My mentor has helped me reach milestones that once felt out of reach, but with his guidance I was able to achieve them. I have grown in so many aspects such as my confidence, time management, and ability to advocate for myself. I wouldn’t be the person I am today without my mentor Ron who believed in my potential and pushed me to grow. I am forever grateful for UStrive and my mentor Ron!


** Explore Colleges Using Our Free Guide
------------------------------------------------------------


** 📘 Want to explore colleges with your student? Download the FREE I’m First! Guide to College—it features 100+ four-year colleges and universities committed to supporting first-generation students. This guide highlights unique programs, resources, and opportunities designed to help your student succeed on their college journey!
------------------------------------------------------------


**
------------------------------------------------------------

Download the FREE Guide (http://email.ustrive.)


Follow Our Socials
https://ustrive.org/

Stay Connected with Us!

Don’t miss out on the latest updates, tips, and inspo—follow us on our social media channels! Whether you're looking for advice, success stories, or just a little extra motivation, our social feeds have got you covered. Join our community and stay in the loop all year round!

Want to change how you receive these emails?
You can update your preferences (https://striveforcollege.us18.list-manage.com/profile?u=e1037ec0f74f5b889d00d768b&id=281e539057&e=6bcfe7458e&c=2587a77959) or unsubscribe (https://striveforcollege.us18.list-manage.com/unsubscribe?u=e1037ec0f74f5b889d00d768b&id=281e539057&t=b&e=6bcfe7458e&c=2587a77959)

subject: Hive Database Federation  ✂️,  Semantic Engineering  🧠,  High Throughput Parquet Parsing 🚀
body_text:
Uber Engineering decentralized its monolithic Hive data warehouse by
implementing Database Federation, migrating datasets into smaller Hive
databases                                                      


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

 TLDR 

 TOGETHER WITH [Confluent] [4]

TLDR DATA 2026-03-02

 UNDERCURRENT: A ONE-DAY CONFERENCE FOR DATA ENGINEERS AND ARCHITECTS.
(SPONSOR) [4] 

 Confluent is hosting a free one-day conference with a catch: there's
no catch. It's a single-track event with no sponsors and no product
pitches—just technical talks for data engineers and architects.

	* 🎙️ Speakers include JOE REIS, HOLDEN KARAU, and MAX BEAUCHEMIN
	* 🚫 No vendors. No sales pitches
	* ✨ 100% free to attend 
	* 📍San Francisco  📅 March 26 
	* 🎟️ Limited to 100 seats — register for free here [4]

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 DATABASE FEDERATION: DECENTRALIZED AND ACL-COMPLIANT HIVE DATABASES
(11 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Uber Engineering decentralized its monolithic Hive data warehouse by
implementing Database Federation, migrating datasets into smaller,
domain or team-owned Hive databases without data duplication or
downtime through a one-time Bootstrap Migrator to copy data to new
HDFS locations and update pointers, while real-time (Apache Flink +
Piper) and batch synchronizers maintained HMS metadata consistency
bidirectionally. 

 HNSW AT SCALE: WHY ADDING MORE DOCUMENTS TO YOUR DATABASE BREAKS RAG
(27 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 When HNSW-based RAG systems exceed around 100K vectors, latency grows
super linearly and recall drops, often returning highly similar but
irrelevant results for rare queries. The causes include local minima
traps, hubness in high dimensions, and memory pressure. Mitigations
include tuning M, ef_construct, and ef_search, using hybrid two-stage
retrieval, applying quantization with oversampling and rescoring, and
relying on optimized engines like Qdrant. 

 INSIDE TENCENT GAMES' REAL-TIME EVENT-DRIVEN ANALYTICS SYSTEM (8
MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Tencent Games implemented a real-time analytics architecture
leveraging CQRS and event sourcing principles, using Apache Pulsar for
high-throughput event ingestion and ScyllaDB to efficiently fan out
events to millions of gameplay sessions. They partition events via
session IDs and leverage ScyllaDB's keyspaces and cross-region data
replication to streamline multi-tenant data management. This design
decouples application logic from data distribution and delivers
low-latency, globally consistent operations for risk monitoring and
in-game moderation. 

 HAVE YOUR CAKE AND DECOMPRESS IT TOO (11 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 SpiralDB's Vortex columnar format implements Cascading Compression, a
recursive, data-driven approach that chains multiple lightweight,
fast-decoding encodings per column. It evaluates schemes on stratified
samples (~1% of data), selects the best greedy path, and recursively
compresses intermediate outputs (codes, dictionaries, and lengths) in
a depth-limited tree to handle skewed, clustered, or mixed
distributions without relying on a fixed codec like ZSTD. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 ANALYTICS ENGINEERING'S UNFINISHED WORK (5 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Analytics engineering is resurging as semantic layers, AI context,
and structured business logic become critical across structural,
measurement, and interpretive tiers. dbt shaped the role but narrowed
it to SQL. With AI agents consuming business logic, ambiguity is
riskier, making strong context engineering and clear semantics
essential to keep data trusted and machine-ready. 

 USING LLMS TO AMPLIFY HUMAN LABELING AND IMPROVE DASH SEARCH
RELEVANCE (6 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 Dropbox enhanced search relevance in Dropbox Dash by combining a
small seed set of high-quality human-labeled query-document relevance
judgments with LLM-assisted labeling to scale training data by ~100x.
Its team tuned LLM prompts on human data to minimize disagreements,
then used the calibrated LLM offline as a "teacher" to generate
massive synthetic labels from error-prone or representative samples. 

 TO LIVE IN AN AI WORLD, KNOWING IS HALF THE BATTLE (28 MINUTE
PODCAST) [11] 

 True human agency in an AI-driven world requires a deep understanding
of algorithms and technology, as people need to move from passive
consumers to active shapers who can critique and improve systems.
Developers should explain ideas clearly, prioritize societal good over
raw speed, and actively redesign tech through curiosity, smart policy,
and responsible choices. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 HARDWOOD: A NEW PARSER FOR APACHE PARQUET (7 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Hardwood is a lightweight, open-source Parquet parser for Java 21+
built for high throughput, multi-threaded reads with minimal
dependencies. Using page-level parallelism, adaptive prefetching, and
memory mapping, it can read 9.2GB or 650M rows in about 1.2 seconds on
16 cores, over 2x faster than row-wise reads, and offers row and
column APIs with broad compression support and planned predicate
pushdown. 

 RIVET (GITHUB REPO) [13] 

 Rivet is a serverless actor platform where each actor has built-in
state, storage, and real-time workflows, letting you run per-user or
per-agent systems that scale from zero to millions with one API. 

 SPACETIMEDB 2.02 RELEASED (GITHUB REPO) [14] 

 SpacetimeDB combines the database and server into one system, running
your app logic inside the database for fast, real-time applications
without separate backend infrastructure. 

 POSTGRESCOMPARE 1.1.104 RELEASED (2 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Schema diffing and deployment automation for Postgres get smoother
with new scripting and dependency-aware features. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 ONTOLOGY DRIVEN DIMENSIONAL MODELING (12 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 Traditional data models and semantic layers strip away real business
meaning, so AI systems end up guessing context and giving confident
but wrong answers. Adding a clear ontology, a structured map of how
the business actually works, enables AI to understand cause and effect
and move from basic reporting to true strategic insight. 

 THE LUNATICS ARE TAKING OVER THE ASYLUM (13 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Agentic AI accelerates code writing but mainly amplifies existing
team maturity: strong teams improve faster, weak teams create more
bugs and risk. The bottleneck shifts to testing, CI/CD, security,
governance, and legacy friction. Expect fewer, higher-skilled
engineers, and better results from leaders who invest in capability
rather than headcount cuts. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 SELECTSTAR (WEBSITE) [18] 

 This Apache Flink SQL and Table API sandbox lets you experiment with
dynamic tables and changelog streams, run live SQL against streaming
data, and see how queries translate between tables and streams in real
time 

 BACKFILLS - THE NECESSARY EVIL OF DATA ENGINEERING (9 MINUTE READ)
[19] 

 Backfills are unavoidable because data changes and bugs happen, but
they are slow, risky, and can damage trust.

body_text:

Hi Rebecca,


Large language models are only as smart as the data you feed them. That’s why retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is such a critical skill to master.

Join us on March 18 at 11am ET for our fourth session in the MongoDB & Python Development Series, MongoDB for Python Builders: RAG <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgfGoouI6jW_023vgZ8-_OVmagm1tfLbkCZrpnbZAnxRSX81Xs8XFgP1ucCfnmDxnO5JWM-Zk=>. We’ll show you how to architect production-ready RAG applications. Uplevel your AI development and learn the following skills:


	- Architecting RAG workflows that ground your LLMs in real-time, proprietary data
	- Optimizing the retrieval process for low-latency, accurate results
	- Managing both vector and original source data within a single, unified data platform



MongoDB experts will be available for 1:1 support to help you troubleshoot issues and answer your questions in live time as we go through hands-on challenges. 

Additionally, you’ll have another opportunity to earn a MongoDB Skill Badge during the workshop that you can add to your LinkedIn profile to showcase your expertise in modern data architecture. 

If you want to catch up on Part 3: MongoDB and Vector Search in 
Python <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgfGoouBNqveoPnqjF6TlIJTz6WIs9O4t90g8TgcFA8RkjUbT3TNdBuYW0gznoAP8bIgRFUyQ=>, the recording is now on-demand. You can also still complete the corresponding Skill 
Badge <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgfGoouFrl5hFo9JEZfDnzYOW0Ed2E_OZqV28GYR5szLQ8j9q5FriiniASS_h5Kv7QZPTze4Q=>.

Ready to start building intelligent software that reasons with your data?
Register now <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgfGoouI6jW_023vgZ8-_OVmagm1tfLbkCZrpnbZAnxRSX81Xs8XFgP1ucCfnmDxnO5JWM-Zk=>
Think Big, Go Far,
The MongoDB Team

subject: Blog Beginning
body_text:
View this post on the web at https://rebeccachoi1.substack.com/p/blog-beginning

Currently sitting in ISEC. My lunch break has now gone on for 1 hour (and counting).
I came here to work with Ivana–I’ve been working on an AI pset and Ivana has also been hard at work (reading her friend’s blog). She did that for a good hour or two. Did some work. and then went back to read it during her “study break”.
It never occurred to me that I could start a blog. It’s such a random thing. Cause who does that. Only millennials from the early days of the internet, as far as I know. But—I used to journal, I like to think. I like to document events through pictures and videos. I have far more thoughts that stay in my head than get voiced. A blog is self-paced, like how I like things. I can take it in whatever creative direction I want. So I realized why not, and that’s how this came to be. I always thought the YouTubers that didn’t post on a consistent schedule but randomly, weeks, sometimes months in between videos were the coolest ones anyway.
I think it’d be cool to document the variety of topics I write about, ranging in depth and seeing the beauty of the juxtaposition of recounts of core memories with random thoughts.
This might just end up being a public journal. It has lowkey already become one lol. But, why not if through it I can share stories of God showing up and working in my life, and if He can be glorified through this!
10 As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God’s varied grace: 11 whoever speaks, as one who speaks oracles of God; whoever serves, as one who serves by the strength that God supplies—in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To him belong glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
1 Peter 4:10-11

All the best,
The Patreon Team

subject: Growth tip: Promote in reader communities
body_text: Growth tip: Promote Rebecca Choi in reader communities To grow Rebecca Choi's readership, you'll want to identify your audience and where to find them. Brainstorm the spaces where current and potential readers congregate. Join these spaces, participate generously, and share your work by showing why it matters to that group. Here are some strategies for finding reader communities: Email a Substack writer with a similar audience. Politely pitch your work to an established writer to ask for a guest post or shoutout. Post in relevant Facebook groups or subreddits. Share your writing with online communities focused on your subject area. What great writers are doing Ali Abouletta of First 1000 sets aside three hours every Thursday to answer questions on Quora and join conversations in relevant Discord servers, WhatsApp groups, and Slack channels. This goodwill helped build a community of advocates for his writing. Read more tips in our guide to developing a publication strategy . subject: SQLMesh Goes Neutral  🤝, Notion’s Vector Search Infra  ⚡,  Speed vs Discipline ⚠️
body_text:
Fivetran is donating SQLMesh (its SQL-based transformation framework
acquired via Tobiko Data last September) to the Linux
Foundation                                                      


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

 TLDR 

TLDR DATA 2026-03-30

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 HOW NOTION SCALED AI Q&A TO MILLIONS OF WORKSPACES (11 MINUTE READ)
[4] 

 Notion's AI Q&A platform scaled to millions of users by evolving its
vector search architecture through dual ingestion, page state
optimization, a serverless migration, and a switch to turbopuffer.
These engineering decisions resulted in a 600x onboarding increase,
60% lower search costs, and p50 latency improving to 50–70ms, while
Ray and Anyscale led to a 90%+ reduction in embeddings infrastructure
costs. The system is now simpler, significantly more cost-efficient,
and supports real-time, semantically rich document retrieval at
enterprise scale. 

 ANALYZING ROUND-TRIP QUERY LATENCY (6 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Instead of just looking at database execution time, Datadog focused
on round-trip query latency with custom-built observability to break
down this latency into components. This revealed hidden bottlenecks
such as connection pool contention, network latency spikes, and
inefficient result handling. 

 HOW TO BUILD TRACEABLE AI WORKFLOWS WITH RETRY AND DLQ VISIBILITY (6
MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Implementing fine-grained, node-based tracing within multi-step
extraction workflows, modeled as an append-only, serializable ledger,
enables deterministic visibility into otherwise opaque LLM-powered
data pipelines. Tracing each decision, retry, and DLQ routing as
distinct nodes not only preserves causal chains and enables efficient,
fine-grained cache invalidation but also transforms debugging and
replayability, allowing teams to precisely audit and re-run extraction
steps without system-wide reprocessing. 

 THE FOUNDATION — WHAT A/B INFRASTRUCTURE ACTUALLY DOES (9 MINUTE
READ) [7] 

 EloElo built a high-performance traffic routing engine that assigns
users to experiment variants in real time, ensures consistent
assignment (stickiness) where needed, tracks metrics, and supports
gradual traffic ramp-ups. The architecture evolved from a memory-heavy
V1 (Redis HashMaps) to an efficient V2 using Redis BitFields (3 bits
per user, sharded for scale), and a stateless V3 for non-sticky
experiments. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 AI IS HERE, BUT THE HARD PARTS HAVEN'T CHANGED (8 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 AI adoption is now nearly universal (99.5% use AI tools, 82% daily or
more), with Claude dominating. However, AI hasn't solved the real hard
part: legacy systems, lack of leadership, poor requirements, and data
modeling and semantic layers. AI speeds up output, but risks creating
more technical debt and "production cesspools" if fundamentals like
context, ownership, and architecture are skipped. 

 ARCHITECTURAL GOVERNANCE AT AI SPEED (12 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 GenAI makes code cheap, but architecture alignment is now the
bottleneck. Traditional governance doesn't scale. The solution is
declarative architecture: encode decisions as machine-readable,
enforceable constraints embedded in dev tooling and made available to
agents (think “Architecture.md”). This shifts governance from
human review to automated guardrails, enabling autonomous teams/agents
while preventing drift. Make the correct path the default path, with
bounded, composable “slices” for safe evolution. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 YOUR PIPELINE WORKS GREAT FOR 3 DATA SOURCES. WILL IT WORK WITH 30?
(SPONSOR) [10] 

 Manage >700 data sources without rebuilding pipelines. Fivetran [11]
delivers analytics-ready data in hours. Fivetran handles: schema
changes, API updates, and retries. You handle: strategy, AI, and
infrastructure overhauls. Free for 14 days, flexible pricing
afterwards. Try Fivetran free [11] 

 FIVETRAN DONATES ITS SQLMESH DATA TRANSFORMATION FRAMEWORK TO THE
LINUX FOUNDATION (2 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Fivetran is donating SQLMesh (its SQL-based transformation framework
acquired via Tobiko Data last September) to the Linux Foundation to
push vendor-neutral governance of the transformation layer. SQLMesh
brings testing, versioning, and Terraform-like plan/apply workflows to
SQL pipelines. The strategic play: shape the open data infrastructure
standard (alongside dbt) and drive adoption via community ownership. 

 DATAHIKE (GITHUB REPO) [13] 

 Datahike is a Datalog-based, immutable, Git-like database: every
write creates a new snapshot you can query, branch, and audit. It
combines time-travel, versioning, and distributed reads (no server
required) with pluggable storage (S3, files, and JDBC). 

 MONITORING YOUR FEAST FEATURE SERVER WITH PROMETHEUS AND GRAFANA (5
MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Feast adds built-in monitoring to the feature server using Prometheus
and OpenTelemetry, making it observable like any production API. Teams
can track latency, throughput, feature retrieval, and system health,
enabling proper SLOs and alerting. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 AI HELPING BUILD BETTER AI: HOW AGENTS ACCELERATE MODEL
EXPERIMENTATION (7 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 LinkedIn built AI agents to accelerate model experimentation and
infrastructure work, particularly for optimizing LLM post-training and
migrating large TensorFlow models to PyTorch. Its flagship agent,
Autopilot for Torch, generates code/configurations, runs automated
verifiers for correctness (trainability, numerical stability, and
metric parity), and receives structured feedback to improve in loops. 

 WHY UUID PRIMARY KEYS QUIETLY DESTROY DATABASE PERFORMANCE (5 MINUTE
READ) [16] 

 Random UUIDv4 primary keys hurt database performance by causing
random inserts, frequent page splits, fragmentation, and poor cache
efficiency in B+ tree storage engines, while time-ordered IDs (like

subject: Growth tip: Share summaries and snippets on social media
body_text: Growth tip: Share a post snippet on social media Congrats on publishing your first post, Rebecca! It's time to share it. Here are a few things you can do to promote your work. Tweet a thread with your post's key takeaways. Encourage readers to subscribe to go deeper. Tell your friends and family why you're starting a Substack. Send an email or Facebook post about your motivation and goals. Share screenshots of memorable quotes to Instagram. Ask followers to comment or message you their emails to get subscribed to your publication. What great writers are doing Judd Legum of Popular Information tweets summaries of his investigative reporting , then asks readers to subscribe for news updates. subject: Searchable Airflow Catalog  🔎, OpenTelemetry Sampling  🧪,  Real-Time Threat Detection  🛡️
body_text:
The Apache Airflow Registry offers a centralized, searchable catalog
of 98 providers and over 1,600 modules, including 848
operators                                                      


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

 TLDR 

TLDR DATA 2026-03-23

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 TLDR DATA #100 - A YEAR IN REVIEW (WEBSITE) [4] 

 100 issues. One year of TLDR Data. This year was shaped by faster
analytical engines, pragmatic database architectures, and real-world
tradeoffs, including those around open data formats. We dug into AI
governance and infrastructure shaping today, and context engineering
and semantic layer patterns emerging next. Dive into the full review
for the highlights and deeper trends. Thanks for reading, building,
and sharing with us. 

 SAMPLING: THE PHILOSOPHER'S STONE OF DISTRIBUTED TRACING (11 MINUTE
READ) [5] 

 Distributed tracing, powered by OpenTelemetry, is essential for
modern observability but generates massive volumes of span data that
outpace current querying capabilities. Sampling (primarily via head or
tail methods) remains vital to control scale and cost: head sampling
offers deterministic, stateless selection, while tail sampling enables
context-aware retention but introduces significant architectural and
operational complexity, particularly in multi-zone environments and
accurate RED metric production. Practical implementations require
smart routing, metric extraction before sampling, and a clear
understanding of trade-offs. Emerging solutions like disk-based
buffering and exemplar-based sampling offer incremental improvements. 

 FROM FIREFIGHTING TO BUILDING: HOW AI AGENTS RESTORED OUR TEAM'S CORE
PRODUCTIVITY (18 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Grab's Analytics Data Warehouse team deployed a multi-agent AI system
to autonomously resolve up to 40% of repetitive user queries,
reclaiming hundreds of engineering hours monthly across their 1,000+
users and 15,000+ tables. Specialized agents—handling tasks from
code enhancement to data lineage investigation—replace manual
triage, while layered safeguards and a human-in-the-loop process
ensure security, data quality, and user trust. 

 MIGRATING ETSY'S DATABASE SHARDING TO VITESS (9 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Etsy migrated from a legacy MySQL sharding setup (single unsharded
index database as a central lookup across 1,000+ tables) to Vitess,
eliminating the index database (a single point of failure), automating
scaling (from months to days), and abstracting sharding complexity
from developers. Its team implemented custom vindexes, rolled out
incrementally table-by-table with quick rollbacks, and achieved
zero-downtime cutover with no massive data movement. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 THE LIVING GRAPH: HOLONS AND THE FOUR-GRAPH MODEL (21 MINUTE READ)
[8] 

 The holonic model introduces a four-layer architecture for RDF
knowledge graphs: interior, boundary/membrane (via SHACL), projection,
and context. This enables true encapsulation, boundary governance, and
contextual relationships. Each holon is both a self-contained entity
and part of a holarchy, facilitating multi-resolution querying,
provenance tracking, and federated authority. Portals enable
controlled, annotated traversal between holons, solving challenges in
representing containment, authority, and navigation that flat RDF
graphs cannot address. This principled structure brings organization,
scalability, and semantic richness crucial for complex, multi-domain
graph systems. 

 THE QUESTION IS THE CONTRACT (17 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Competency questions are explicit, domain-specific queries that a
system must answer. Systems built without first defining and
maintaining these questions often yield inaccurate or incomplete
results, because architectural decisions default to implicit
assumptions rather than clear requirements. Leveraging competency
questions provides a rigorous, testable framework that guides schema
design, validates coverage, and ensures traceable, actionable answers
in everything from vector databases and knowledge graphs to
retrieval-augmented generation pipelines. 

 AI IS REDRAWING THE DATABASE MARKET (13 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 AI workloads are forcing a convergence of previously separate domains
(real-time analytics, data warehousing, and observability) into a
single high-concurrency, low-latency, full-fidelity data platform, as
legacy batch-oriented systems can't handle bursts of concurrent
interactive queries, massive unsampled data needs, or real-time
freshness without failing. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 INTRODUCING THE APACHE AIRFLOW REGISTRY (2 MINUTE READ) [11] 

 The Apache Airflow Registry offers a centralized, searchable catalog
of 98 providers and over 1,600 modules, including 848 operators, 298
hooks, and 372 modules for Amazon alone. Features include instant
search (Cmd+K), provider-specific pages with one-click install
commands, integrated connection builders generating URI, JSON, or Env
Var formats, and a JSON API for programmatic integration with tools
and IDEs. This streamlines module discovery, configuration, and
automation. 

 HOW ROOST IS ADVANCING ONLINE SAFETY (7 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Discord donated its internal high-performance rules engine, Osprey
(now production-ready and community-improved), to ROOST. It processes
real-time platform events (logins, messages, and account changes) to
detect threats instantly, evaluate thousands of rules across actions,
flag suspicious activity, and support investigations with managed
services from partners like Musubi and Zentropi. 

 QCON LONDON 2026: INTRODUCING TANSU.IO - RETHINKING KAFKA FOR LEAN
OPERATIONS (4 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 Tansu.io introduces a Kafka-compatible, stateless messaging broker
where durability shifts entirely to external storage, radically
reducing broker memory footprint (~20MB) and enabling instant
scale-to-zero deployments within 10ms. With pluggable storage backends
(S3, SQLite, or direct Postgres), Tansu simplifies streaming pipelines
by writing validated records (Avro, JSON, or Protobuf) directly to
open table formats like Iceberg and Delta Lake, and eliminates the
transactional outbox. Code available on GitHub. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 NEOCLOUDS AND WHY AI COMPUTE DEMAND HAS OUTGROWN HYPERSCALER BALANCE
SHEETS (7 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Hyperscalers' growth (now near cash flow ceilings) cannot keep pace,
making neoclouds indispensable overflow valves in a structurally
supply-constrained, geography-bound market. AI compute demand has
caused Azure's backlog to surge 1,150% to $625B, yet even Microsoft
cannot self-supply, driving rapid partnerships with neoclouds like
CoreWeave and Crusoe, whose combined GPU commitments now exceed $131B.
Large AI labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic now diversify away from
single-cloud dependence, while neoclouds provide 10–20% of AI capex.


 5 PRODUCTION SCALING CHALLENGES FOR AGENTIC AI IN 2026 (4 MINUTE
READ) [15] 

 Moving autonomous agentic AI systems from impressive demos to
reliable production remains far harder than traditional ML, due to
amplified issues in coordination, visibility, economics, testing, and
control. Probabilistic outputs break deterministic testing. Emerging
LLM-as-judge and simulations help, but still need heavy human
oversight and lack standardization. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 SHIPPING AT THE RIGHT PACE WITH AI TOOLS (2 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 AI makes it wildly easy to ship, but users cannot keep up if you
expand too fast and pile on sloppy features. 

 TURNING LIMIT INTO AN I/O OPTIMIZATION: INSIDE DATAFUSION'S
MULTI-LAYER PRUNING STACK (5 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Limit pruning exploits SQL LIMIT clauses to skip entire Parquet row
groups, cutting I/O and boosting query speed.

subject: UStrive Mentee Newsletter - March 2026
body_text:
View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/b67eb757d563/ustrive-mentee-newsletter-march-2026?e=6bcfe7458e)
http://app.myustrive.com

Hi Rebecca,

Welcome to the March edition of the UStrive newsletter! In case you missed it, UStrive 2.0 (http://app.myustrive.com/login) is now live. In this newsletter, you’ll find out information about the new version, information about what it means to be waitlisted, an exclusive UStrive scholarship opportunity, a chance to have your resume reviewed, our product updates, dates to look out for in April, this month’s mentor & mentee highlight, and more!

Keep reading to learn more,

The UStrive Team

UStrive 2.0

Earlier this month, we fully sunsetted UStrive 1.0 and all user data has been migrated to our new version — 2.0! You should have received an email with the subject line, "Welcome to the New UStrive Portal – Your Login Details Inside." It contains the temporary password needed to log in to the new portal. If you never received the email, no problem! Simply email us at support@ustrive.com (mailto:support@ustrive.com) and we'll get you up and running.

If you haven't already, please watch this quick 3-minute video that provides an overview of what 2.0 offers and how to navigate the platform: (https://youtu.be/3b7eLloFDws?si=UKlRoTcsUautCu6D)

https://youtu.be/1eaW1WdVKbs?si=bYtJS8BS5yl8uKVr

Have You Been Waitlisted?

Here’s What you Need to Know

If you’re applying to selective colleges, you might find yourself on a waitlist. This means the school isn’t ready to offer you a spot right away, but there’s a chance space could open up later. Being waitlisted doesn’t mean you’re not qualified or not good enough. Many top schools receive far more qualified applicants than they can accept because they simply don’t have enough room—whether in classrooms, dining halls, or residence halls!

Click on the following article to learn how you can navigate the process: https://ustrive.co/waitlist-article

Seniors,

College acceptance season is here, and we want to celebrate this huge milestone with you! Whether you’re jumping for joy, tearing up, or sharing the moment with family and friends, we want to see your genuine reaction as you open your college acceptance letter.

Record a video of yourself opening your acceptance, send it to us, and 5 lucky winners will each receive $500 towards their college expenses!

Here's how to set up for a great video:
1. Position your phone horizontally - make sure we can see and hear you.
2. Let your true emotions shine through - we want to see your genuine reaction!
3. Keep the camera rolling before and after you open your acceptance - we'll take care of the editing.
4. Your video can feature your friends and family cheering you on, or just yourself.

Don't miss out on this opportunity to showcase your excitement and potentially win some extra cash for college! Submit your video using the link below before the deadline on April 9, 2026.

Submit Your Video Here: [https://ustrive.typeform.com/to/Kc4202g4 (https://www.google.com/url?q=https://ustrive.typeform.com/to/Kc4202g4&sa=D&source=editors&ust=1774568496246012&usg=AOvVaw2tXmua3vQMU4UinMwul9Tf) ]

**Please ensure that videos are in their original format and free from any personal or company branding**

We can’t wait to celebrate with you—good luck! 🥳🎓

Resume Review

This fall, we will be sending 150 resumes to mentors at our corporate partners, including Deloitte, UBS, Clearsulting, and more! The mentors will write their feedback, and UStrive will send it to you by June 19. Don’t wait! Our first round of reviews begins in April, and early submissions can expect to receive their feedback sooner.

SUBMIT HERE (https://ustrive.typeform.com/to/AjAMMxMT)

Please remove all personal information including last name, email, and school name from your resume before submitting.

UStrive Product Updates


** Now You Can Control Your Notification Settings!
------------------------------------------------------------

We've added communication preferences to your account settings. You can now choose how and when you'd like to receive updates from us. Visit your UStrive Settings (http://app.myustrive.com/login) via the web portal to manage your preferences at any time.


** You Can Click on a Mentor’s Name to Connect With Them in the “Community” Tab
------------------------------------------------------------

If you've ever posted in the "Community" tab and a mentor replied back saying they can help you, you can now click on their name and request them as a mentor! Simply click on their name, select the "Request Mentor" button, and the mentor will receive the request.

Note: If you do not see the button for a mentor, it is either because you are currently matched with a mentor (mentees are currently limited to working with one mentor at a time), their availability is turned off, or your domestic/international status doesn't match what they’ve indicated they can help with.

Scholarships

Missed a few scholarship deadlines? It happens. The good news: it’s not too late to find money for college. Spend a few minutes searching on Fastweb (https://www.fastweb.com/?utm_source=QRCode&utm_medium=Referral&utm_campaign=2025-26_EDU) or College Board’s BigFuture (https://ustrive.co/bigfuture) . Fastweb lists thousands of scholarships, and BigFuture lets you enter monthly drawings for $500 and $40,000 awards just by completing simple college‑planning steps. It’s free, easy, and could pay off big.

Tips:

Apply for as many scholarships as possible—small amounts add up!

Stay organized by tracking deadlines and requirements. You can create a document within your “Mentoring” tab.

Have your mentor review your applications to ensure you highlight your strengths and experiences.

Never pay for scholarship searches—scholarship scams exist!

Start early—some scholarships open a year in advance.

Pro Tip: Local scholarships (offered by Rotary Clubs, businesses, and schools) often have fewer applicants, increasing your chances of winning!

Get More Info & Apply: Log in to your UStrive account and head to the Pay for College (https://ustrive.myustrive.com/mentor/resource-hub/guides/130idkfntUGCUjYTYviPdm?guideCategory=HIGH_SCHOOL) section in our Guides tab for a full list of resources, search tools, and expert tips to help you secure funding!


** Mentor & Mentee Highlight
------------------------------------------------------------

Mentee: Emily C.

Why did you decide to join UStrive?

I decided to join UStrive because I needed guidance. As a first-generation college student, I didn’t have people around me who could guide me through the college journey. Finding UStrive has been such a blessing!

What has been the most impactful part of mentoring with UStrive?

There are so many impactful parts of mentoring with UStrive, but the most impactful part has been having a mentor who believes in my potential. My mentor has helped me reach milestones that once felt out of reach, but with his guidance I was able to achieve them. I have grown in so many aspects such as my confidence, time management, and ability to advocate for myself. I wouldn’t be the person I am today without my mentor Ron who believed in my potential and pushed me to grow. I am forever grateful for UStrive and my mentor Ron!

If you could share any advice with other mentees, what would it be?

My advice for other mentees would be to be intentional during your mentoring sessions. Come prepared with any burning topics or questions you want to discuss. Arriving on time and communicating with your mentor ahead of time if you need to reschedule is very important. Being intentional not only shows respect for your mentor’s time, but it also helps you get the most out of the mentoring sessions!

Mentor: Ron L.

Why did you decide to join UStrive as a mentor?

I was open to volunteering and had actually applied to Big Brother Big Sister, but they took a long time to respond. At the time, I was working at Deloitte, and UStrive had a mentorship program I could participate in through the company's community contribution initiative. I also realized that UStrive had a very fast matchmaking system — I was able to get my first mentee within one week of joining and had our first video call within two weeks. This was amazing! On top of that, it was the age group I was hoping for: seniors in high school who are genuinely first-generation college students, for whom this would be their first real experience with the college journey since their parents didn't attend college.

What has been the most impactful part of mentoring with UStrive?

The most impactful part is sharing tips and techniques with students that took me many years to learn — things like understanding what HR recruiters are looking for and how to time block. These are huge for them.

 TOGETHER WITH [Aquata] [4]

TLDR DATA 2026-03-16

 TRADE HOURS OF MANUAL ENGINEERING FOR PRE-BUILT CONNECTORS. (SPONSOR)
[4] 

 Instead of manually connecting investment data that arrives in
multiple formats and constantly maintaining it, you could be putting
that data to work. The Aquata® Data Platform replaces months of
tedious ETL engineering with pre-built connectors that automatically
normalize and validate that data for you, with:  

	* Pre-built connectors to custodians, fund admins, market data, and
cloud platforms  

	* Domain-specific investment data models  

	* Automated schema mapping and validation  

	* Faster onboarding of new data sources  

Meet the data connectivity layer for investment teams. GET A FREE
30-DAY TRIAL [4].

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 ENGINEERING THE NEXT GENERATION OF LINKEDIN'S FEED (12 MINUTE READ)
[5] 

 LinkedIn redesigned its feed by introducing a unified retrieval
system powered by LLM-generated embeddings and a sequential Generative
Recommender (GR) model using causal attention transformers to model
chronological interaction sequences, capturing deeper semantic
relevance and professional trajectories without relying on demographic
features. 

 INSIDE THE ARCHIVE: THE TECH BEHIND YOUR 2025 WRAPPED HIGHLIGHTS (12
MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Spotify's Wrapped Archive identifies up to five “remarkable days”
in each user's listening history using heuristics and data pipelines,
then generates personalized narratives grounded in the data using a
fine-tuned LLM. To scale to ~1.4 billion reports, Spotify distilled a
smaller model, built distributed pipelines and storage optimized for
concurrency, and used automated LLM-based evaluation to ensure
accuracy, safety, and consistency at launch. 

 HOW DID YOUTUBE ENGINEERS BUILD CI/CD FOR DATA PIPELINES? (8 MINUTE
READ) [7] 

 YouTube's data warehouse processes multiple exabytes daily across
thousands of time-partitioned pipelines, demanding robust CI/CD
practices to address dynamic data schemas, intricate dependencies, and
distributed observability. Its framework leverages test configuration
isolation, dependency-aware configuration rewriting, sampling to
reduce test data by up to 99.9%, and a centralized metadata hub for
enhanced collaboration and traceability. This approach delivers up to
50% faster integration investigations, shrinks schema deployment
cycles from months to weeks, and improves overall data quality and
cross-team velocity. 

 TEST SMARTER, NOT HARDER: RISK-BASED DATA QUALITY WITHOUT PIPELINE
PARALYSIS (11 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Vinted adopted a risk-based testing approach inspired by prioritizing
impact and informational quality, tagging dbt tests with
impact/frequency levels, excluding low-impact ones from main dbt
builds, and running high-impact tests daily via Airflow while
monitoring others weekly or via alerts. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 MCP IS DEAD; LONG LIVE MCP! (9 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Claims that MCP is obsolete are mostly hype: while CLIs can sometimes
save tokens, they face similar context and usability limits when tools
are custom. For organizations, MCP remains valuable because it
provides structure, security, telemetry, and centralized tooling
needed to run AI agents reliably at scale. 

 THE CONTEXT PROBLEM (25 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 AI vendors monetize “context” as a billing unit, charging by
token count rather than the quality or coherence of information
processed, with prices varying up to 360x between major models (e.g.,
GPT-5.4 Pro at $180/million output tokens vs. Grok 4.1 Fast at $0.50).
Expanding context windows often degrades model performance unless
context is well-structured. Context engineering, neurosymbolic AI, and
knowledge graphs can cut token usage by up to 80%. Invest in explicit
semantic structures and context governance to avoid skyrocketing AI
spend and unreliable outputs. 

 YOUR DATA MODEL ISN'T BROKEN, PART I: WHY REFACTORING BEATS
REBUILDING (12 MINUTE READ) [11] 

 Big-bang rewrites of legacy data systems, often triggered by new
leadership or platform migrations, consistently underestimate
essential business complexity and the institutional knowledge embedded
in existing models. Refactoring (small, incremental improvements with
rigorous testing) preserves critical, undocumented logic and avoids
the 45% average IT project overrun and 56% value shortfall documented
by McKinsey. Treat legacy complexity as indispensable knowledge,
methodically improve it, and avoid discarding years of hard-earned
operational understanding. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 KIP-1150 ACCEPTED, AND THE ROAD AHEAD (8 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 KIP-1150's approval brings Diskless Topics to Apache Kafka, enabling
compute-storage separation by shifting replication and storage from
broker disks to cloud object storage. This transformation slashes
total cost of ownership by up to 80%, eliminates inter-AZ replication
traffic, and allows for instant elasticity without client changes.
This major change positions Kafka as a truly cloud-native streaming
standard. 

 OPENVIKING (GITHUB REPO) [13] 

 OpenViking is an open-source context database designed specifically
for AI agents (such as OpenClaw). OpenViking unifies the management of
context (memory, resources, and skills) that Agents need through a
file system paradigm, enabling hierarchical context delivery and
self-evolving. 

 DOLT (GITHUB REPO) [14] 

 Dolt is an open-source MySQL-compatible database with built-in
Git-style version control. It lets you branch, diff, merge, commit,
and clone tables and schema just like code in Git, while remaining
compatible with standard SQL tools. Useful for data collaboration,
reproducibility, auditing, and debugging, you can inspect historical
states of datasets and resolve row-level merge conflicts directly in
SQL. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 EVOLUTIONARY DATABASE DESIGN (31 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Evolutionary database design enables agile teams to iteratively
evolve database schemas alongside application code by leveraging
automated migration scripts, rigorous version control, and continuous
integration pipelines. Key practices include treating all schema and
data changes as versioned migrations, automating database provisioning
for every developer and environment, and ensuring frequent, small,
reversible changes with close collaboration between DBAs and
developers. This approach scales to hundreds of developers and
database instances without increasing DBA headcount, significantly
reducing release risk and supporting uninterrupted 24/7 operations. 

 DATA MANAGEMENT PRINCIPLES FOR RESILIENT SYSTEMS (13 MINUTE READ)
[16] 

 True resilience arises from how systems interact under stress, not
from isolated data assets or individual component strength. Effective
data management demands that data seamlessly flows into
decision-capable systems with well-designed integrations, rapid
governance pathways under duress, and clear operational authority.
System diagrams often mask hidden dependencies and integration
weaknesses, which only manifest during crises. Investing in
integration-first design, real stress simulations, and adaptive
governance ensures technical and organizational optionality. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 SYNTHETIC DATA, REAL HARM (9 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Synthetic data addresses challenges of data scarcity, fairness, and
privacy in AI development by enabling dataset augmentation, reducing
bias, and bypassing regulatory hurdles, but introduces risks of data
pollution, model collapse, and subtle privacy breaches. 

 RUNPOD REPORT: QWEN HAS OVERTAKEN META'S LLAMA AS THE MOST-DEPLOYED
SELF-HOSTED LLM (4 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 Runpod's analysis of anonymized AI infrastructure logs from over
500,000 developers reveals Qwen has surpassed Llama as the
most-deployed self-hosted LLM, despite Llama's higher visibility.

subject: Entry 1: Why a Blog
body_text:
View this post on the web at https://rebeccachoi1.substack.com/p/entry-1-why-a-blog

Currently sitting in ISEC. My lunch break has now gone on for 1 hour (and counting).
I came here to work with Ivana–I’ve been working on an AI pset and Ivana has also been hard at work (reading her friend’s blog). She did that for a good hour or two. Did some work. and then went back to read it during her “study break”.
It never occurred to me that I could start a blog. It’s such a random thing. Cause who does that? Only millennials from the early days of the internet, basically. But—I used to journal, I like to think. I like to document events through pictures and videos. I have far more thoughts that stay in my head than get voiced. A blog is self-paced, like how I like things. I can take it in whatever creative direction I want. So I realized why not, and that’s how this came to be. I always thought the YouTubers that didn’t post on a consistent schedule but randomly, weeks, sometimes months in between videos were the coolest ones anyway.
I think it’d be cool to document the variety of topics I write about, ranging in depth and seeing the beauty of the juxtaposition of recounts of core memories with random thoughts.
This might just end up being a public journal. It has lowkey already become one lol. But, why not if through it I can share stories of God showing up and working in my life, and if He can be glorified through this!
10 As each has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace: 11 whoever speaks, as one who speaks oracles of God; whoever serves, as one who serves by the strength that God supplies—in order that in everything God may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To him belong glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
1 Peter 4:10-11
