Reddit migrated its petabyte-scale Apache Kafka fleet with over 500
brokers from Amazon EC2 to Kubernetes without any downtime or data
loss                                                      


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

 TLDR 

TLDR DATA 2026-03-19

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 HOW REDDIT MIGRATED PETABYTE-SCALE KAFKA FROM EC2 TO KUBERNETES (9
MINUTE READ) [4] 

 Reddit migrated its petabyte-scale Apache Kafka fleet with over 500
brokers from Amazon EC2 to Kubernetes without any downtime, data loss,
or client-side changes. It achieved this by introducing a DNS facade
for seamless connection abstraction, doubling cluster size with
higher-ID EC2 brokers to free low IDs, and forking Strimzi operator
for mixed EC2-Kubernetes operation. 

 RANKING ENGINEER AGENT (REA): THE AUTONOMOUS AI AGENT ACCELERATING
META'S ADS RANKING INNOVATION (6 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Meta's Ranking Engineer Agent (REA) is an AI agent that accelerates
ads ranking by managing the full ML lifecycle with almost no human
input. REA uses the Confucius framework for persistent state and tool
access. It generates high-quality hypotheses from historical insights
with ML Research Agent by following a Three-Phase Planning Framework
(Validation → Combination → Exploitation) within compute budgets
and handling errors autonomously via runbooks. 

 HOW WE OPTIMIZED DASH'S RELEVANCE JUDGE WITH DSPY (10 MINUTE READ)
[6] 

 Using DSPy's optimizer, Dropbox defined a clear objective (minimize
normalized mean squared error against human judgments), incorporated
structured feedback from rating gaps and human rationales, enforced
JSON validity guardrails, and ran iterative prompt refinement,
enabling 10-100x more synthetic labeling at the same cost, and
accelerating model switches from weeks to 1-2 days. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 CLAUDE CODE ISN'T GOING TO REPLACE DATA ENGINEERS (YET) (8 MINUTE
READ) [7] 

 Claude Code is a powerful productivity booster for rapid prototyping,
iteration, and handling repetitive tasks in data engineering, but it
lacks the judgment, trust, and reliability needed for unsupervised
production work due to confident-yet-wrong outputs, silent data loss,
and non-determinism, making it a strong "companion" tool today rather
than a replacement. 

 DISPATCHES FROM THE GARTNER DATA & ANALYTICS SUMMIT 2026: THE NOISE,
THE SLOP, AND THE SIGNAL (10 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 AI adoption has accelerated dramatically, with agents now generating
write-heavy, contextual "trajectory" data that strains traditional
operational databases and blurs boundaries between infrastructure and
feature stores. Real-world deployments, such as OpenAI's scaling of
PostgreSQL to 800 million users and insurers leveraging 95% accurate
speech-to-text for rapid care plan creation, highlight measurable ROI.
AI governance has become urgent, requiring new guardrails atop
existing data governance, while the hype around context graphs signals
growing complexity and unresolved semantic integration challenges. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 YOUR CEO HAS QUESTIONS ABOUT THE DATA. CAN SHE ANSWER THEM? (SPONSOR)
[9] 

 The way people ask questions has changed. With Starburst's AIDA [9],
every employee from analyst to CEO can explore enterprise data in
plain language, run complex analyses, and apply their own business
rules in real time. No SQL. No tickets. No BI backlog. Meet AIDA, your
AI data assistant [9] 

 PGIT: WHAT IF YOUR GIT HISTORY WAS A SQL DATABASE? (13 MINUTE READ)
[10] 

 pgit is a Git-like CLI that stores repositories in PostgreSQL with
built-in delta compression, making the entire commit history
SQL-queryable while often matching or beating Git's best compression.
It enables powerful codebase analysis, allowing developers and AI
agents to instantly query history, detect patterns, and generate
insights without custom tooling. 

 GREENBOOST — 3-TIER GPU MEMORY EXTENSION FOR LINUX (GITLAB REPO)
[11] 

 GreenBoost is an open-source Linux kernel module and CUDA shim that
extends GPU VRAM using system RAM and NVMe, allowing large AI models
to run on smaller GPUs without modifying inference code. It works by
intercepting CUDA memory allocations and transparently offloading
overflow to slower memory tiers, trading some performance for
significantly increased capacity. 

 TIGERFS (TOOL) [12] 

 TigerFS is a system that mounts a PostgreSQL database as a
filesystem, letting agents and humans read and write shared data as
files with full ACID transactions and version history. It replaces
fragile file-based coordination by combining the simplicity of files
with the reliability, structure, and concurrency of a database. 

 METABASE (GITHUB REPO) [13] 

 Metabase is an open-source business intelligence platform that lets
teams query, visualize, and share data without heavy tooling. It
connects to many databases, supports SQL and no-code exploration, and
provides dashboards, alerts, and embedding. It offers a lightweight,
self-hostable analytics layer that reduces dependency on complex BI
stacks while enabling governed, accessible data exploration. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 ARE AI AGENTS ACTUALLY SLOWING US DOWN? (9 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Heavy reliance on AI coding tools at tech giants like Anthropic,
Amazon, Uber, and Meta is driving significant increases in code output
(engineers classified as "power users" of AI produce 52% more pull
requests), but is also leading to notable declines in software
quality, increased outages, and growing technical debt. At Anthropic,
80%+ of production code is AI-generated, resulting in critical UX bugs
impacting millions, while Amazon has seen a rise in SEVs and now
mandates senior review of AI-assisted code. These trends highlight the
need for stronger architectural oversight, code validation, and
emphasis on quality assurance. 

 GITGUARDIAN REPORTS AN 81% SURGE OF AI-SERVICE LEAKS AS 29M SECRETS
HIT PUBLIC GITHUB (4 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 AI-assisted coding drove a 34% year-over-year surge in leaked secrets
in 2025, with Claude Code commits showing a 3.2% leak rate (over twice
the 1.5% baseline) resulting in nearly 29 million exposed credentials
detected on GitHub. Leaks involving AI service credentials jumped 81%
year-over-year, and internal repositories were six times more likely
to contain hardcoded secrets. Persistent remediation gaps (64% of
valid secrets from 2022 still unrecalled) highlight critical
governance and NHI management shortfalls. 

 SNOWFLAKE CORTEX AI ESCAPES SANDBOX AND EXECUTES MALWARE (11 MINUTE
READ) [16] 

 Modern AI agents across tools like Snowflake Cortex, Copilot, Claude,
and Slack are vulnerable to prompt injection attacks that can bypass
safeguards, execute malware, and exfiltrate sensitive data. A real
example shows how an injected prompt tricked Cortex into running
malicious code outside its sandbox without user approval, enabling
attackers to steal or destroy data using the victim's credentials. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 SNAP DECISIONS: HOW OPEN LIBRARIES FOR ACCELERATED DATA PROCESSING
BOOST A/B TESTING FOR SNAPCHAT (4 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Snap has migrated its A/B testing data pipelines for Snapchat,
processing over 10 PB of data per day, from CPU-based Apache Spark to
NVIDIA GPU-accelerated Spark on Google Kubernetes Engine, realizing 4x
faster runtimes and 76% daily cost savings. 

 AI BLIND SPOT DEBT THREATENS GOVERNANCE (3 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 Unmanaged models create hidden technical debt.

subject: Claude Builds Data Apps  🦆,  Rust-Powered Stream SQL  🦀,  Safe Data Garbage Collection 🧹
body_text:
With Claude Code connected to MotherDuck’s MCP server for live data
access, anyone can quickly build custom, interactive, refreshable data
apps                                                      


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

 TLDR 

TLDR DATA 2026-03-09

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 GARBAGE DAY: HOW PINECONE SAFELY DELETES BILLIONS OF OBJECTS AT SCALE
(9 MINUTE READ) [4] 

 Pinecone uses immutable storage where every write creates a new file,
which leaves behind stale or orphaned data that increases storage
costs. They built Janitor, a system that safely identifies, verifies,
and deletes unused objects at scale using cautious multi-phase checks
and auditability to avoid deleting data still in use. 

 MACHINE LEARNING WITH ADBC, DUCKDB & XGBOOST: NO PANDAS, JUST PURE
ARROW TABLES (21 MINUTE VIDEO) [5] 

 This walkthrough shows a practical ML workflow where ADBC pulls data
from DuckLake as Arrow tables directly into XGBoost, with SQL handling
preprocessing and PyArrow handling the train/test split instead of
Pandas or scikit-learn. The main point is that ADBC and Arrow can
simplify and standardize database-to-ML pipelines with fewer libraries
and a cleaner, more portable workflow. 

 UNIFIED CONTEXT-INTENT EMBEDDINGS FOR SCALABLE TEXT-TO-SQL (17 MINUTE
READ) [6] 

 Pinterest's Analytics Agent transforms data discovery and Text-to-SQL
by leveraging 2,500+ analysts' query history, governance metadata, and
AI-generated documentation into a centralized, semantically searchable
knowledge base. By embedding SQL intent and structural patterns, the
system delivers context-aware, asset-first analytics, achieving 40%
user adoption, cutting documentation effort by 70%, and dramatically
improving query reliability and data trust. 

 THE PRACTICAL LIMITS OF DUCKDB ON COMMODITY HARDWARE (9 MINUTE READ)
[7] 

 DuckDB delivers warehouse-style, columnar analytics with sub-second
performance on datasets up to 5 million rows and remains comfortably
interactive for GROUP BY and percentile queries up to 10 million rows,
even on $500 laptops (16GB RAM). On this setup, window functions
become noticeably slower beyond 10M rows (1.7s at 5M, 6s at 10M, ~1
minute at 50M rows). Memory usage remains modest (<1.2GB for 50M
rows), making the 1M-20M zone the sweet spot for local interactive
analytics with DuckDB on consumer laptops. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 CLAUDE CODE + DIVES = ANY DATA UI (11 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 With Claude Code connected to MotherDuck's MCP server for live data
access, anyone can quickly build custom, interactive, refreshable data
apps and visualizations as shareable “Dives” (React files with
embedded live SQL queries), iterate rapidly using diff previews, and
publish them directly in MotherDuck for team use. 

 IT'S ABOUT THE STRATEGY, STUPID (15 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Most analytics work focuses on tactics (tools, audits, and tracking
improvements) without asking how the data will actually support
business strategy. Effective analytics starts by understanding the
company's goals and decisions first, then designing data and metrics
that directly support those strategic priorities. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 YOUR CEO HAS QUESTIONS ABOUT THE DATA. CAN SHE ANSWER THEM? (SPONSOR)
[10] 

 The way people ask questions has changed. With Starburst's AIDA [10],
every employee from analyst to CEO can explore enterprise data in
plain language, run complex analyses, and apply their own business
rules in real time. No SQL. No tickets. No BI backlog. Meet AIDA, your
AI data assistant [10] 

 FELDERA (GITHUB REPO) [11] 

 Feldera is a query engine for incremental computation written in
Rust. It continuously updates materialized views from inserts,
updates, and deletes instead of recomputing everything. It supports
full SQL, handles larger-than-memory data, connects to sources like
Kafka, S3, CDC, and warehouses, and provides strong consistency so
results match equivalent batch execution, with low-latency,
high-throughput processing for real-time analytics and ETL workloads
at scale. 

 SKORE IS LIVE: TRACK YOUR DATA SCIENCE (8 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Skore is an open-source layer around scikit-learn focused on model
evaluation, comparison, and experiment/report persistence for teams.
It reduces evaluation boilerplate, adds methodological guardrails, and
makes collaboration more reproducible. Skore means cleaner handoffs
from notebooks to production through structured artifacts, metrics,
and project-level tracking. 

 INSIDE THE FLIGHT PATH OF REAL-TIME INGESTION IN APACHE PINOT (13
MINUTE READ) [13] 

 To guarantee a single consistent "winning" segment across multiple
Pinot server replicas consuming the same Kafka partition, Pinot uses a
lightweight controller-orchestrated blocking commit protocol where the
controller elects a committer based on the max offset, while
non-committers discard locals and download the official version. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 SCALING TO 120+ AI AGENTS WITHOUT LOSING CONTROL (23 MINUTE READ)
[14] 

 Switch to a multi-agent system with a conductor-specialists pattern
when scaling beyond 15 tools or 3 conflicting domains. Multi-agent
design maximizes per-task quality but adds orchestration complexity,
hybrid retrieval outperforms single approaches, and tightly-scoped
tool profiles reduce token waste. Example architecture: VoltAgent for
orchestration, SurrealDB for unified vector/graph/relational storage,
hybrid retrieval (0.6 vector, 0.2 graph, 0.2 keyword), and cost
control via dynamic task routing (with Haiku for classification). 

 ANTHROPIC'S COMPUTE ADVANTAGE: WHY SILICON STRATEGY IS BECOMING AN AI
MOAT (11 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Anthropic has established a structurally superior, diversified
compute stack (leveraging AWS Trainium2 and Google TPUv7) delivering
30–60% lower per-token costs than Nvidia-only configurations and
enabling 2+ gigawatts of dedicated capacity. This architecture,
secured through $52 billion in long-term commitments with Broadcom,
AWS, and Google, grants Anthropic unmatched negotiating leverage,
cost-efficiency, and iteration speed. In contrast, OpenAI and
Microsoft remain largely dependent on Nvidia, facing significantly
higher inference costs and delayed internal silicon programs. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 PANDAS VS. POLARS: A COMPLETE COMPARISON OF SYNTAX, SPEED, AND MEMORY
(5 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 Pandas is more intuitive for exploratory analysis, while Polars uses
expressions and lazy evaluation to optimize queries, making it better
suited for high-performance, large-scale data engineering and
production workloads. 

 STOP TUNING HYPERPARAMETERS. START TUNING YOUR PROBLEM (14 MINUTE
READ) [17] 

 Over 80% of ML failures come from poor problem framing, not bad
models or data.

subject: Jesus
body_text:
View this post on the web at https://rebeccachoi1.substack.com/p/jesus

Would I rather be with __(person)__ or have Jesus? Jesus
What’s better: working at Google / __top company__ or having Jesus? Jesus
Would I rather be mega successful and liked by all or have Jesus? Jesus all the way
How great is it that I do have Jesus. How great is it that Jesus is my savior!
The past few months I’ve been trying to be more intentional about when and how I listen to worship music. There was a point when it was basically the only type of music I listened to but I wasn’t actually listening to the words. My heart wasn’t really engaged; it’d just be playing in the background and sometimes I’d really vibe with the musicality of the song. But rarely was I actually listening to the lyrics and thinking about what they meant. So I started to ration my worship music. I stopped myself from just listening out of habit rather than for what it was: worship. Songs of praise to God.
Glad to say that my relationship with worship music has gotten much better and I’ve started to listen to certain songs that I didn’t previously like that much more, simply for the lyrics.
It’s been particularly helpful being reminded of who Jesus really is and what it means for us.
Jesus is my healer, he’s everything I need.
He alone has triumphed over sickness and disease
Fear where is your power? The cross is your defeat
Jesus is My Healer, Gateway Worship (2023)
Jesus is king over ALL. Fear where is your power? 🗣️
I know it was the blood
Could have only been the blood
The Blood, Bethel Music (2024)
Could’ve only been the blood of Jesus that cleansed and saved me. Not me, not anything I did, not whatever image I gave off, just the blood.
Jesus is the answer for the world today
Above him there’s no other, Jesus is the way
Jesus Is The Answer, Andraé Crouch (1993)
I was thinking about my non-Christian friends with this one along with all other non-believers. Jesus is the answer, not any myth that the world tries to sell them. Not a job, not never lacking in money, not always being happy, not even a great friend group. Jesus is what (who) they’re looking for.
I don’t want anything but you
You’re more than every dream come true
All of the things I thought I wanted
Don’t come close to knowing you
Give Me Jesus, Bethel Music (2024)
I want to just live for Jesus, freely.
I realized this recently when I found myself liking someone and getting caught up wondering if he liked me. Does he? Nah. Wait. Does he? And then wondering if he would also want to move overseas and go on missions right after graduation. lol.. and then it clicked. I realized: I don’t need him to do it with me. I’d still do it with or without him. It wasn’t even him I wanted most, it was following after God. All I really wanted was to be fully, wholly committed to God, and to truly know Jesus.
Life has lots of silly games. Jobs, love interests, hobbies. Granted, some all of these are actually important. But for things to chase after, to make your life goal, they’re just so silly in comparison to what it means to know Jesus.

 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

 TLDR 

 TOGETHER WITH [AWS] [4]

TLDR DATA 2026-03-12

 BUILD RAG APPS FASTER WITH UNIFIED DATA MANAGEMENT (SPONSOR) [4] 

 Managing data across platforms slows ML development and increases
operational overhead. This tutorial [4] shows how Amazon Redshift,
Amazon Bedrock, and Databricks work together to streamline your data
infrastructure.

 * QUERY EFFICIENTLY: Access Redshift directly from Databricks
notebooks without ETL pipelines
 * AUTOMATE VECTORIZATION: Transform structured data into vector
embeddings for AI applications
 * SCALE RAG APPS: Integrate Bedrock foundation models for
production-ready retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)

Explore practical solutions for optimizing data access and ML
workflows in AWS Marketplace.

READ THE TUTORIAL → [4]

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 DRIVING DATA ENHANCEMENT & RECRUITMENT SUCCESS WITH LINKEDIN'S
UNIFIED INTEGRATIONS (14 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Using a declarative transformation layer, Temporal for orchestration,
Kafka for streaming, Espresso for persistence, and support for both
partner-push (BuildIn) and LinkedIn-pull/push (BuildOut) models with
idempotent, secure, observable flows, LinkedIn cut partner onboarding
time by 72%, expanded data coverage 4x, boosted data completeness, and
provided a stable, governed foundation for features like LinkedIn's
Hiring Assistant. 

 BUILDING HIGH THROUGHPUT PAYMENT ACCOUNT PROCESSING (9 MINUTE READ)
[6] 

 To handle extreme "hot-key" traffic on high-activity payment accounts
which previously hit sequential processing limits of 3–4 ops/sec per
account, causing multi-hour processing times for bulk jobs, Uber uses
a three-service architecture to batch financial updates into ~250 ms
windows (using Redis for coordination/queuing) with an atomic write
per batch, and offloads immutable audit logs asynchronously. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 YOUR PIPELINE SUCCEEDED. YOUR DATA DIDN'T (12 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 A BigQuery-native anomaly detection system can catch silent data loss
by monitoring ingestion volume across hundreds of tables using only
built-in features like INFORMATION_SCHEMA logs and
AI.DETECT_ANOMALIES. Implemented as a single dbt model, it detects
abnormal drops in data volume without external tooling or per-table
rules, helping teams identify partial pipeline failures that
traditional pipeline success checks miss. 

 HOW I IMPROVED MY ANALYTICS AGENT RELIABILITY FROM 45% TO 86% (15
MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Analyzing failures in an analytics agent and fixing issues in tests,
date-selection rules, documentation, and especially the underlying
data model improved reliability from 45% to 86%. The results show that
most gains in context engineering come from clearer data models,
explicit rules, and better documentation rather than complex agent
architectures. 

 DATA CONTRACTS WON'T SAVE YOU IF YOUR AI AGENT CAN'T READ THEM (8
MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Traditional data contracts and governance policies, written for human
oversight, are largely invisible to AI-powered machine consumers,
exposing organizations to undetected errors and policy breaches.
Contract controls like freshness SLAs, usage restrictions, quality
thresholds, and semantic definitions are typically stored in config
files and documentation, making them inaccessible to autonomous agents
at query time. Critical governance elements must transition from
human-readable specifications to machine-readable, queryable metadata
and enforceable runtime policies. 

 SILENT DATA LOSS IN CLICKHOUSE: 3 REASONS YOUR DISTRIBUTED QUEUE
KEEPS GROWING (7 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 Inserts into ClickHouse Distributed tables seem to succeed instantly
but silently pile up as .bin files in an on-disk queue that never
reaches the underlying ReplicatedMergeTree tables, causing permanent
data loss and missing rows. The root causes include ClickHouse Keeper
downtime putting replicas into read-only mode and stalling background
flushes, as well as oversized insert blocks killing the flush and
blocking the entire queue. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 CONNECT YOUR FIRST DATA SOURCE IN <10 MINUTES WITH 700+ PREBUILT
CONNECTORS FROM FIVETRAN (SPONSOR) [11] 

 Working with an ever-growing set of data sources that don't talk to
one another? Spend your time on something other than wrangling APIs.
Fivetran's [12] free trial includes over 700 connectors, allowing you
to replace manual integrations with zero-maintenance data automation.
Try it today [12] — no credit card needed [12]. 

 ANNOUNCING DUCKDB 1.5.0 (16 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 DuckDB v1.5.0 introduces major advancements, including a reworked
CLI, support for the VARIANT type (with binary storage for enhanced
compression and query performance), and the elevation of GEOMETRY to a
native core type with automatic column shredding—reducing storage by
up to 3x. Notable concurrency and aggregate optimizations yield a 17%
TPC-H SF100 throughput boost and up to 40% faster aggregates. 

 SCALING WITH AIRFLOW 3.2: WHEN TO DEFER AND WHEN TO USE NATIVE ASYNC
OPERATORS (8 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Apache Airflow 3.2 adds native async support to PythonOperator,
allowing high-throughput I/O workloads to run concurrently inside a
single worker without triggerer overhead. Combined with Dynamic Task
Iteration, this approach dramatically improves performance for
micro-batch tasks like API calls or SFTP transfers. 

 ORCHESTRATE DBT CORE IN PRODUCTION WITH KESTRA (5 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Kestra orchestrates dbt Core transformations by integrating
scheduling, dependency management, retries, and alerting within a
declarative YAML-based workflow. Its 1,200+ plugin ecosystem enables
end-to-end orchestration across ingestion, transformation, and
activation layers, while providing full cross-stack lineage tracking
with Assets. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 LEAKYLOOKER: HACKING GOOGLE CLOUD'S DATA VIA DANGEROUS LOOKER STUDIO
VULNERABILITIES (10 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 Tenable Research uncovered nine critical cross-tenant
vulnerabilities, dubbed "LeakyLooker," in Google Looker Studio,
exposing organizations' data across BigQuery, Sheets, and other GCP
connectors to exfiltration and manipulation. These flaws enabled
attackers to exploit credential handling and SQL injection vectors to
access, modify, or steal data with zero or one click, breaking
established BI platform trust boundaries. Google has remediated all
vulnerabilities. 

 TOP AI GITHUB REPOSITORIES IN 2026 (10 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Most impactful open-source AI projects include OpenClaw (210k+ stars,
fastest-growing ever local AI assistant with 50+ integrations and
self-extending skills), Ollama (local LLM runtime that enables
privacy-focused on-device models), n8n, Langflow, Dify, LangChain, and
more, reflecting 2026 trends toward local/privacy-first AI and agentic
autonomy. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 GITTRENDS (WEBSITE) [18] 

 A Google Trends style view of the GitHub ecosystem, powered by
ClickHouse. 

 YOUR DATA AGENTS NEED CONTEXT (7 MINUTE READ) [19] 

 Data agents are only useful when grounded in a well-maintained
context layer that captures business definitions, source of truth
data, governance rules, and tribal knowledge so they can answer real
questions reliably.

We're introducing one login to connect Glassdoor and Indeed accounts. Continue with one login When you connect accounts, your recent profile data will be synced, giving you access to better job matches and hiring employers across both sites. Our commitment to anonymity Your anonymous activity on Glassdoor, like company reviews or demographic information, won't be shared with Indeed and will remain anonymous. What's next For right now, you’ll need to connect accounts to apply to jobs on Glassdoor and get improved job matching. Starting on April 20th, 2026, you may be required to log in with a connected account to get full access to Glassdoor. You can access your profile data or delete your account any time. subject: Filter of Hope: March Gladness and Beyond
body_text:
Stories of health and hope are streaming in

March Gladness is Going On!

There are 89 teams heading out this month to communities across Latin America. Because of partners like you, clean water and the gospel will be shared in thousands of homes in partnership with local churches. Two of the stories shared in this email came from these trips. A couple of the stories are incomplete—the storytellers are too busy delivering more filters!

Going Over Water to Give Water

College teams bring health and hope to a Guatemalan island

The Table Was Set

Winston was ready

When Excursions Change Lives

FamilyLife and Filter of Hope team up to help families

Pray for Spring Break Trips

89 teams are delivering clean water and the gospel

Going Over Water to Give Water

College teams bring health and hope to a Guatemalan island

Sometimes people who are surrounded by water still have great difficulty in getting access to clean water.

That’s what a Cru team from Duke University and Mandy Pelton, a Filter of Hope staff member, discovered on their mission trip to southern Guatemala.

Mandy says that the municipal government on the island of Las Lisas had requested their visit. “They had recently realized that many residents were suffering from a common parasite. They needed clean water immediately.”

During the “March Gladness” season, all of the teams that stay with Fe Viva ministry in Guazacapán will go to Las Lisas. Then the last week a medical team will visit the island to help with the parasite treatment. Total eradication is the goal.

They had recently realized that many residents were suffering from a common parasite. They needed clean water immediately.

Adding to the adventure of going to an island was also the mode of transportation—vintage (well-used) boats!

It Wasn't an Island Paradise

Mandy and her team met Elizabeth and her granddaughter, Deborah in one of the homes they visited that week on Las Lisas. As the team got to know this family they came to understand that parasites weren’t the only thing that made life difficult in this island community.

“Elizabeth told us there were only two types of work on this island—fishing, which can be inconsistent and expensive, and bricklaying. Though almost everyone was born and raised here, many also can’t stay because they can’t find work.”

Elizabeth quickly understood that the water filter would help not only with their health, but also their finances. “She was grateful.”

Needing Hope

Her positivity carried over when the team shared the gospel with her. “She was eagerly engaged as we shared how the filter represents the hope we have through the Living Water, Jesus.”

She was eagerly engaged as we shared how the filter represents the hope we have through the Living Water, Jesus.

Elizabeth also saw her need.

“We asked her what would happen if she died—would she go to heaven? On a scale of 1 to 10, how sure was she that she would go to heaven? She told us she was a ‘0.’”

The team explained that no one can earn their way into heaven and that it was a gift from God. Because Jesus died for all sins, when someone puts their trust in Him, all of their sins are forgiven. Redemption is complete and eternal life is certain.

Elizabeth said that she wanted to receive Christ. “One of the team members named Olivea led her in a prayer to accept Christ.”

God is at Work

A harmful parasite had brought the team to Elizabeth's home. But before they left, she had received both clean water—and the hope of new life in Christ.

“What a sweet gift from the Lord to get to be the ones who shared with her the hope she could have in Him. We left her home having encountered God once again at work long, long before we stepped out of the boat.”

The Table Was Set

Winston was ready

Before our mission teams arrive, the local church knocks on doors to prepare families for their visits. So the teams know that families are waiting for them with their buckets close by.

No one was more ready than Winston.

The mission team from Acts 2 Boston and Filter of Hope staff member Maggie Mulder were going to homes near Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic. They dropped by Winston’s home and soon began installing the water filter so he could have clean water in his own house.

Winston appreciated having clean water for his family, but Maggie says he immediately thought of another use for the water filter.

“A large group from the community plays basketball every evening for many hours and he planned to bring the filter with him so that they can all have clean water.”

But Winston was ready for much more than clean water.

After wrapping up the filter installation, the team began sharing the gospel. “Winston immediately got excited.”

The team discovered the reason for Winston's enthusiasm when he threw out a truly amazing statement. “He said he had decided he wanted to accept Christ 20 days earlier, but he didn't know how.”

The group had a very interested listener and they took their time to help him understand what it meant to receive Christ.

“We were able to break down the gospel with him and share what his next steps were after accepting Christ.” It was an evangelistic, follow up, and discipleship visit all in one.

One of those next steps they talked about was fellowship with other believers. “We also helped him know how to connect with the local church.”

God had everything prepared. “The Lord brought us to him today in perfect timing.”

When Excursion Change Lives

FamilyLife and Filter of Hope team up to help families

Each February on the FamilyLife (a Cru ministry) cruise, couples can choose a Filter of Hope outreach as one of their excursion options. This year, Chuck Roeper, a Filter of Hope staff member, and his wife Dianne took part in the cruise so they could help train and lead couples as they visited homes to share clean water and the gospel.

148 cruise participants joined in the outreach excursion.

This was also a special day for Chuck and Dianne for another reason. This was the first time that Dianne had been able to participate in a Filter of Hope outreach in the six years Chuck had worked for Filter of Hope.

Chuck and Dianne led one of these outreaches in Cozumel, Mexico. “My group visited the home of a grandmother with two grandsons, one a teenager and the other in elementary school.”

The filter especially caught the eye of the teenager. “He was very curious about the filter and how it worked.”

He was hooked. "When I communicated the gospel using Scripture and water and filter analogies, he listened intently.”

But it wasn’t just the teenager who was interested. “I explained their need to repent and receive Christ and they all did. It was such a joy to see all three of them make the decision to accept Christ!”

Chuck went on to ask some follow up questions and their clear, heartfelt answers showed that they understood what they were doing.

"When we were leaving, the teenager thanked us for coming and telling them about Jesus."

As they said goodbye, Dianne received a sweet expression of Latin American hospitality.

“The teenager gave Dianne a kiss on her cheek.”

subject: Meet the new LinkedIn Hiring Pro.
body_text:
It's more than a job post. It's your AI hiring partner.
 2.7 million small businesses have used LinkedIn to hire in the last 12 months.¹ Post a free job Hi Rebecca, Hiring is tough when you're already stretched thin. That’s where LinkedIn Hiring Pro helps. It's AI that works like the recruiter you wish you had — screening applicants, shortlisting the best fits, and surfacing candidates you may not have found on job boards. With LinkedIn Hiring Pro, you can: Discover unique talent. Hiring Pro taps into LinkedIn’s network to surface qualified candidates who aren't actively searching, but are open to new opportunities. Spend time on only the right people. Hiring Pro evaluates applicants using LinkedIn’s real-time data to create a pre-vetted shortlist. Make hiring faster and easier. Hiring Pro helps with posting, sorting, and screening so hiring stays manageable even when you’re busy. Post a free job Happy hiring, Will from LinkedIn ¹ Based on LinkedIn Global data, representing small businesses who have used LinkedIn to hire in the last 12 months (December 2025) This email was intended for Rebecca Choi (CS & Design @ Northeastern University) Learn why we included this.
